newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Large Kazakh commercial bank has licence withdrawn.
newsitem.headline: Large Kazakh commercial bank has licence withdrawn.

text.p: Kazakhstan's AO KRAMDS Bank, the first commercial bank founded in the central Asian republic and one of the largest, has had its licence withdrawn, a National Bank of Kazakhstan spokesman said on Monday.
"We have withdrawn the licence of KRAMDS Bank," Toksinjan Rakhimov, deputy head of the department charged with withdrawing bank licences at the National Bank of Kazakhstan, told Reuters on Monday.
He said the decision was taken late on Friday. Urazaly Erzhanov, deputy chairman of the national bank, has been appointed to head a commission overseeing the liquidation of KRAMDS Bank.
The National Bank of Kazakhstan did not give an immediate reason for the move, saying it would give more details in a news conference later on Monday.
There was no immediate comment from KRAMDS Bank.
A crowd of worried depositors gathered outside the modern glass and steel headquarters on Monday morning in the centre of Almaty.

"They (KRAMDS) didn't warn us and they acted like looters," said Irina Shershova, 62 and standing in the crowd. She had placed 120,000 Kazakh tenge (about $1,700) with the bank hoping to earn annual interest of 27 percent. "This is the last money we have," she said.
The bank was founded in 1989 and was said by the banking community to be highly active in Kazakhstan's nascent foreign exchange and debt markets.
In July, the National Bank of Kazakhstan warned the former Soviet republic's 102 struggling banks they had to bring capital ratios up to global standards or face closure.
"It's their choice to die immediately or sometime later," Grigory Marchenko, deputy chairman of the National Bank of Kazakhstan, said in an interview last July.
KRAMDS is around the 30th bank to be closed this year but one of the biggest names.
The bank's deputy chairman, Alexander Yakushev, told Reuters in July that he was convinced his bank would succeed in restructuring.
